items.title: Lockheed Martin (LMT) Marks First Saudi F 35 Push And Germany F 35A Rollout
items.summary: Lockheed Martin (NYSE:LMT) is set to benefit from a US government plan to sell up to 48 F-35 jets to Saudi Arabia, following a notification to Congress in 2026. The proposed Saudi package would mark the first sale of F-35 aircraft to the kingdom, expanding US fifth generation fighter exports in the Gulf. Lockheed Martin also marked the rollout of Germany's first F-35A in 2026, a key step in Berlin's transition to the aircraft. The initial Saudi F-35 sale and Germany's first F-35A rollout...

items.title: He Left SpaceX to Rebuild the American Factory
items.summary: A single replacement part for one of the Air Force's most important cargo planes can take four years to build. A former SpaceX engineer just proved his robots can make one in two months.*How scrappy startups take on industries worth billions:* https://clickhubspot.com/nxmiEd Mehr left SpaceX and Relativity Space to solve a problem that had nothing to do with software: manufacturing can't move at software speed. His fix, Machina Labs, replaces the custom, million-dollar "dies" that traditional stamping relies on with two robotic arms that can shape sheet metal into almost anything — no new tooling required. It's already caught the attention of the US Air Force, NASA, and Lockheed Martin, who's betting on Machina to help diversify a defense supply chain where 87% of programs cite supply-chain issues as a bottleneck to scaling. The tradeoff is speed — Machina can't out-produce a stamping line yet — but the company is betting that flexibility, not volume, is what modern manufacturing, and modern warfare, actually needs.In this series, our producer and host, Noelle Medina, gets an inside look at the small yet scaling companies quietly reinventing America's biggest industries.Check out our other episodes here: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLblFs6y75WUv7UtwrOApsHasI_YkauabF0:00 The four‑year replacement‑part problem0:38 Why traditional stamping dies make factories slow, rigid, and insanely expensive2:53 Ed Mehr’s path through SpaceX & Relativity Space 3:47 Founding Machina Labs to build a new kind of flexible, robot‑run factory5:30 Meet the RoboCraftsman7:12 Inside Mach 2: upgraded arms, swappable “warheads,” and containerized factory cells8:07 Two‑layer software & real‑time feedback that lets robots sculpt metal like human hands12:00 Where Machina actually wins13:03 Defense pivot15:53 Expressive customization and an off‑planet “teal workforce” futureGet the 5-minute newsletter keeping 2M+ innovators in the loop: https://thehustle.co/join-free-2

items.title: Can A Faster Factory Lift Boeing Stock?
items.summary: Boeing (BA) stock is down about 8% over the past year and trades about 22% below its 52-week high. Inside the factories the picture reads differently: the company is delivering airplanes at a pace it has not managed since 2018, against a record order book. The upside case rests on a clear assumption: translating that delivery pace into positive free cash flow.

items.title: Is RKLB Stock Paying You Enough For The Swings?
items.summary: Rocket Lab (RKLB) has gained 9.5% over the last five trading days, while the S&P 500 added 0.6%. A week like that pulls money in. The stock is still about 55% below its 52-week high. The run is not the question. What matters for your money is what this stock does to your portfolio when the market moves, because it travels about four times as far as the index in both directions.
